question: Is the 267 ms per-evaluation loss time at 8937 bright-field terms a hardware floor for the exact objective, or merely the current implementation's number? Specifically: (a) what is the best achievable time for the loss path's device_memory traffic measured independently of the engine, (b) was the previously reported 266 ms two-pass prediction derived independently or circularly, and (c) if pure-traffic time is materially below 267 ms, where is the exposed time and is there a bit-exact fix?

parameters.host_load_range: 3.1-4.9; every timing set is paired against the other arm in the same lock hold

execution.gpu_model: Apple M5 10-core GPU, 24 GB unified memory
execution.contention_note: All runs taken under the shared GPU lock with GPU_RUN_LABEL=anscombe-metal-floor. Host load is quoted with every timing set; the real loss and the traffic ceiling were interleaved ABBA in the same lock hold so that load drift cancels.

results.verdict: CONFIRMED, with the previous wording corrected. The 267 ms objective is not merely the current implementation's number, but the real headroom is 5-14 ms per evaluation (2-5%), not the 26% (16 s) implied by comparing the circular 105.7 GB/s aggregate against a per-pass best rate. The 26% prize does not exist.

circularity_check.finding: CIRCULAR. The 266 ms two-pass prediction is algebraically identical to the 267.1 ms measurement it was said to validate.
circularity_check.arithmetic: 105.7 GB/s = 28.223188992 GB / 0.2671 s, and 266 ms = 28.223188992 GB / 105.7 GB/s = 0.26701 s. The 'prediction' is the measurement restated to three significant figures.
circularity_check.quoted_source: experiments/20260916-metal-ssb-fit-acceleration/manifest.json:251 ("two_pass_model_prediction_ms": 266) and the same file's conclusion string at line 256 ("The 2-pass model predicts 28.23 GB at the observed 105.7 GB/s aggregate, i.e. 266 ms against 267.1 ms measured.")
circularity_check.what_survives: The independent part of that earlier argument is the 4-pass exclusion: 47.04 GB floors at 339 ms (column rate 138.8 GB/s) or 406 ms (row rate 115.7 GB/s), both well above the measured 267.1 ms. That exclusion uses per-pass rates from a different measurement and is not circular. The error was only in presenting the 2-pass restatement as a confirmation.

independent_traffic_ceiling_ms_best_of_f.note: Never below 226.98 ms in eight independent best-of-five sets. This is the floor for the loss path's memory traffic with trivial compute, which no bit-exact implementation of the objective can beat.

exposed_time_budget_ms.method: Each category isolated by adding exactly one real feature to the traffic kernel and re-measuring best-of-five in the same lock hold.

dispatch_gaps.evidence: 2236 empty dispatches = 1.58 ms, 3354 = 1.93 ms (~0.6 us/dispatch); full3 with three dispatches per batch (232.95) is within noise of full with two (228.56-234.39). REFUTED as a contributor.

row_threadgroup_memory_occupancy.evidence: rowtg adds the real kernel's 26752 B of threadgroup memory (scratch 4x512 + tile 4x324 of the 32768 B budget) and the same staged access pattern: 77.11 ms vs row 76.41 ms. REFUTED as a contributor.

row_fft_arithmetic.evidence: rowfft 82.49 ms (real radix-8 inverse FFT, helper copied verbatim from ssb.metal) vs row 76.23 ms.

atan2_transcendental.evidence: rowatan2 93.42 ms (8 variable-argument atan2 per thread per bright-field term = 2.34e9 per evaluation) vs rowfft 82.49 ms. A cheaper probe using a constant denominator was strength-reduced by the compiler and is not valid evidence.

nyquist_boundary_loads_and_phase_accumul.evidence: rowfull 104.25 ms (adds the Nyquist boundary loads, Hermitian mirror and eight sum/sumsq accumulators) vs rowatan2 93.42 ms.

row_pass_total_exposed.note: A faithful replica of the row kernel's mandatory instruction mix reaches 104.25 ms, within 5.5 ms of the real row pass, so the row pass is within 5% of the cost of its own necessary computation.

column_pass.note: The real column pass is FASTER than the trivial traffic replica, so 149.5 ms is the better estimate and there is no column headroom to claim.

nyquist_pass.evidence: Ablation-derived 9.1 ms; run in isolation it costs 9.0 ms, i.e. the pass is 100% serialized and overlaps with nothing. 1118 dispatches of only 16 threadgroups of 64 threads = 1024 threads in flight, roughly 10% occupancy, so it is latency- rather than throughput-bound.

achievable_floor.statement: At most 13.5 ms per evaluation, essentially all of it the Nyquist pass's latency-bound serialization, against the 16 s (26%) the circular arithmetic suggested.

bit_exact_fix_attempt.arm: Fold the Nyquist dispatch into the column dispatch grid (grid 257x8 -> 259x8, branch on group.x), which is bit-exact by construction: identical per-element arithmetic, same command buffer, no summation-order change, no row bright-field split.
bit_exact_fix_attempt.result: REJECTED on measurement - the fused grid is 5.3-5.7 ms SLOWER than the separate-dispatch form.
bit_exact_fix_attempt.caveat: The probe carried trivial work in the Nyquist-shaped dispatch, so it priced the grid-shape cost of fusion rather than the real Nyquist work. It therefore does not falsify Nyquist batching; it does show that folding the dispatch in without changing its parallelism buys nothing.
bit_exact_fix_attempt.remaining_priced_option: Batch the Nyquist dispatch across 32 bright-field terms instead of 8 (4x the threadgroups per dispatch, bit-exact per bright-field term) to restore parallelism; expected recovery ~6-7 ms, i.e. ~1.5 s of a 62 s fit (2.5%). Requires a source change to encodeFusedCachedPhaseLoss and a 4x Nyquist buffer; NOT attempted, because a 2.5% gain does not justify touching a frozen-precision path.
bit_exact_fix_attempt.conclusion: No bit-exact route to a meaningful saving exists. The atan2 (10.9 ms), FFT (6.3 ms) and Nyquist epilogue (10.8 ms) are the objective's own arithmetic and cannot be reduced without changing what is computed.

outputs.result: Independent traffic-only ceiling harness (standalone Metal, no engine): streams the exact loss geometry - 8937 bright-field terms, G read 1052672 B/BF, blocked-4-row ring write, ring read, phase-sum RMW - with trivial compute. Modes: read/write/col/row/full plus rowfft/rowatan2/rowfull instruction-mix replicas, null2236/null3354 dispatch-overhead probes, rowtg threadgroup-memory probe and nyqsep/nyqfused Nyquist-shape probes.

Dispatch-shape and pass decomposition under the lock at load 3.4-4.9: null2236 1.58 ms and null3354 1.93 ms for 2236/3354 empty dispatches; full3 (three dispatches per batch) 232.95 ms vs full (two dispatches) 228.56-234.39 ms; read 78.95-84.64, write 57.35, col 153.31-158.30, row 76.23-77.33, full best 228.56 ms. Paired ABBA against the real loss path.
Gated pass ablation at matched load plus paired ceiling: real loss p50 268.3 ms; nyquist 9.1, column 149.5, rows 109.7 ms derived additively; ceiling col 153.31, row 77.33, full 231.27 ms.

Row-pass attribution at load 3.7-4.1: row 76.41, rowfft (real radix-8 inverse FFT) 82.27, rowfull (faithful replica of the row kernel instruction mix) 104.83, rowatan 76.99, rowtg (26752 B threadgroup memory) 77.11 ms.
Atan2 split and Nyquist fusion probe at load 3.9: row 76.23, rowfft 82.49, rowatan2 (real variable-argument atan2) 93.42, rowfull 104.25 ms; full 231.42, nyqsep 230.05, nyqfused 235.36/235.73 ms.
Nyquist pass in isolation at load 3.1-3.3: nyquist-only 9.0 ms p50 versus its 9.1 ms in-situ contribution, i.e. the pass is fully serialized; gated full 270.4-275.6 ms; paired ceiling full 226.98 ms.
Real loss path, four paired ABBA runs at load 4.0-4.9: 20 warm samples min 263.9, p50 268.0, max 288.3 ms; loss values bit-identical across all runs; prepare 2.00-2.09 s; allocated 11.36 GB.
